chunks: And what prevented their spending from being accepted from them was that they disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and they did not come to prayer except while sluggish, and they did not spend except while grudging.
ai.seo_question: Why were the charitable donations of the hypocrites not accepted in Islam?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to highlight the distinction between mere outward ritualism and inner sincerity (ikhlas), particularly regarding the hypocrites (munaqiqun) of Medina. The three deficiencies—faith, prayer, and charity—are viewed as interconnected pillars where spiritual lethargy and reluctance reveal a deeper disconnect between the heart and the limbs. This underscores the principle that acts of worship are only accepted when accompanied by conscious devotion and voluntary generosity.
